title: One-Eye, Two-Eyes, Three-Eyes
summary: Little Two-Eyes was despised by her sisters One-Eye and Three-Eyes because she looked like ordinary humans. They gave her rags and crusts....
full_text:
Little Two-Eyes was despised by her sisters One-Eye and Three-Eyes because she looked like ordinary humans. They gave her rags and crusts.

A wise woman gave her a magical goat: saying "Little goat, bleat, little table spread!" produced a golden feast.

When the cruel sisters discovered the secret and slaughtered the goat, Two-Eyes buried its entrails before the house.

From the earth sprang a magnificent tree with leaves of silver and apples of solid gold! The proud sisters could not pluck a single apple—the branches leaped away. But when Two-Eyes reached out, the golden apples bent into her hand.

A noble knight rode by, fell in love with her gentle modesty, and took her to his castle, while the tree followed her and planted itself outside her palace window!
moral: Those despised for being normal and gentle are blessed with golden fruit and true love.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "One-Eye, Two-Eyes, Three-Eyes (Einäuglein, Zweiäuglein, Dreiäuglein)"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
